title: Customer Commitment Bucketizer and Sprint Allocation
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Top-account escalations and VIP intake frequently arrive mid-cycle. We lack a consistent, auditable mechanism to translate those signals into sprint-level capacity (what we call 'commitment slots') without either over-allocating runway to noise or violating enterprise commitments. This ticket defines and implements the 'Commitment Bucketizer' — a scoring and allocation service that converts account signals (escalation severity, ARR, strategic fit, product-signal alignment, legal/compliance constraints) into discrete sprint buckets for PM/ENG capacity planning.

Goals:
- Create a transparent scoring model that yields a numeric priority score and bucket assignment (FastTrack, High-Touch, Watchlist, Backlog) for incoming requests.
- Surface per-sprint recommended allocation (number of ticket-days / story points) and the reasoned justification for each bucket assignment.
- Provide automatic SLA-triggered escalation paths (e.g., urgent security/regulatory issues => immediate FastTrack) with audit trail.
- Enable periodic rebalancing: if multiple FastTrack items exceed reserved capacity, the model proposes degraded-commitment options or trade-off candidates.

Scope:
- Design score schema and weight matrix (configurable in Console) — initial weights: EscalationSeverity 35%, ARR 25%, StrategicFit 20%, ProductImpact 10%, TimeSensitivity 10%.
- Implement a service prototype (stateless scoring microservice) + lightweight UI in Console Intake (PM view) showing bucket, raw score, and recommendation.
- Integrate with Priority Router: output bucket metadata into intake record so it feeds downstream workflows (SRE on-call, Solutions Eng, Sales Ops).
- Expose audit log and decision explanation for each assignment (why weight contributed).

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We prefer a simple weighted linear model initially to maximize transparency and speed-to-value. ML ranking could follow in a future cycle once we collect 6+ months of labeled decisions.
- Default ARR bandings use $ thresholds but allow account teams to override; overrides are logged and require secondary approval for FastTrack.
- To avoid blocking normal sprint planning, FastTrack allocations are limited to a configurable percentage (default 15%) of sprint capacity; the rest is handled via canary/fallback model with explicit rollback runbooks.

Acceptance Criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Deliverables/Artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/CR-commitment-bucketizer-proposal
- Prototype UI mockups (Design): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/commitment-bucketizer-designs
- Scoring service repo (initial PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/priority-bucketizer/pull/12
- Intake dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.com/dashboards/intake-buckets

Risks:
- Perception risk: customers may see automatic bucket assignment as gating; mitigate via transparency and manual appeal flow.
- Operational risk: mis-weighted scores could over-index on ARR; include guard rails and monthly calibration.

Success criteria (first 3 months):
- 70% reduction in time-to-decision for VIP intake (manual triage time down to <24h).
- 90% of FastTrack assignments have an associated remediation plan or committed scope in the upcoming 2 sprints.
- Stakeholder satisfaction (Sales/CS/Revenue) >= 4/5 in a post-launch survey.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring model documented and review-approved by PM/ENG/Design
Console intake shows bucket, score breakdown, and 'appeal' link
PR merged for scoring service and e2e tests for weight calculation
Auto-binding of bucket metadata into Linear intake records via API
Config flag for FastTrack capacity percentage with default = 15%
Audit log entries for all manual overrides with approver and rationale
success_metrics: % FastTrack items with committed scope in 2 sprints >= 90%
Monthly calibration drift < 8% between model score and manual override rate
